The ACES Act is a critical step in addressing the silent crisis of military aviator cancers—a long-overdue reckoning with toxic exposures our heroes face. While fully funding veterans' healthcare is non-negotiable, let’s not ignore the systemic failure that necessitated this study. Why did it take decades of skyrocketing cancer rates before Congress acted?

The $55 million allocated for this research must produce actionable results, not just another report collecting dust. True accountability means using these findings to overhaul safety protocols and fast-track benefits for affected aircrews.

Every dollar spent should translate to lives saved, not bureaucratic box-checking. Our warriors deserve prevention, not just post-diagnosis care.

The real test is whether this funding finally forces the Pentagon and Congress to confront the root causes—see the full breakdown: https://t.co/vu8cenPh68
@RepPfluger @POTUS You left out Army Aviators and I personally know two fellow helicopter pilots who died of glioblastoma. Wish you would tell us why you left out Army Aviators.

The ACES Act is a critical step toward addressing the alarming cancer rates among military aviators—aircrew face a 24% higher cancer risk than civilians. While the study mandated by H.R. 530 Section 2(a) is necessary, the real test is whether the VA executes it without bureaucratic delays. The bill requires the Secretary to finalize agreements within 60 days or face reporting obligations, but history shows agencies often drag their feet.

Taxpayers deserve transparency: every dollar allocated must bypass D.C. bloat and directly serve veterans. Prioritizing health outcomes over paperwork is non-negotiable.

Now enforce the deadlines.

The $50B Rural Health Transformation Program under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act is exactly how Washington should work—redirecting funds from bloated bureaucracies to critical needs like rural healthcare. This isn’t just spending; it’s strategic investment in American communities.

By prioritizing preventative care, workforce retention, and tech innovation, the program tackles systemic inefficiencies that left rural hospitals crumbling under Biden. Critics calling this “big government” miss the point: real reform means cutting waste elsewhere to fund sustainable solutions.

The focus on state-driven metrics ensures accountability—no more blank checks for failed urban pet projects. A win for fiscal discipline AND rural America.

See how the numbers stack up and what’s really changing for rural hospitals: https://t.co/D8En6ZRzLP
